items.title: Confidence Score Guided Incremental and Speaker Adaptive Pseudo-Labeling for Semi-Supervised Elderly Speech Recognition
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel confidence score guided incremental and speaker adaptive pseudo-labeling approach for semi-supervised elderly speech recognition. It facilitates higher-quality pseudo-label selection and progressive refinement, while also mitigating speaker heterogeneity. A confidence estimation module is designed to rank the reliability of untranscribed data, enabling a curriculum learning trajectory that progressively folds in unlabeled data subsets from high to low confidence. Speaker-specific characteristics are captured through speaker adaptive training with learnable prompts. Experiments on the English DementiaBank Pitt and Cantonese JCCOCC MoCA elderly speech datasets suggest that the proposed method outperforms the semi-supervised baseline using no confidence scores guided incremental or speaker adaptive pseudo-labeling by statistically significant word error rate (WER) or character error rate (CER) reductions of 1.45% and 2.27% absolute (6.21% and 6.98% relative).

items.llm_tldr_cn: 老人语音识别面临数据不足和说话人差异大的问题。本文提出置信度分数引导的增量式说话人自适应伪标注方法，包括置信度评估模块实现课程学习，以及说话人自适应训练。在英语和粤语老人语音数据集上的实验表明方法有效提升了半监督识别性能。
